paragraphs.dominant_move: open with a human-scale congestion cost -> explicit output -> next handoff
state the infrastructure design target and spatial focus -> explicit output -> next handoff
justify assumptions as a modeling bridge -> explicit output -> next handoff
diagnose the baseline before proposing alternatives -> explicit output -> next handoff
name CTM and WAM as generated candidates -> explicit output -> next handoff
explain the shared release-time mechanism -> explicit output -> next handoff
establish the practical benefit of highways -> explicit output -> next handoff
introduce the funding reason for toll collection -> explicit output -> next handoff
identify the booth-to-lane merge mechanism -> explicit output -> next handoff

global_organization_chain: A six-paragraph research-flow abstract that selects CTM in general and announces later reliability checks.
A direct recommendation built around one-second-safe release spacing and a claimed all-aspect advantage.
A three-paragraph chain: three-objective context -> formal deliverables -> literature-based design decisions.
A conditional operating regime in which the release and merge recurrences can be written.
A reusable symbol table feeding kinematics, geometry, throughput, risk, and cost.
A diagnosed baseline whose failures motivate a release-time controller rather than only new lane markings.
A control rule plus a two-arc merge geometry and near-even booth-to-lane allocation; for B=8,L=3, D=105.5 m and three optimal patterns are reported.
A competing CTM variant with a waiting buffer and an explicit later evaluation promise.
A reported near-tie between EM and CTM, a roughly 1.6 veh/h WAM gain, and a decision to discard WAM because the land cost outweighs the gain.
A claimed 13.66% CTM reduction and one-second PET floor, accompanied by a Table 2 label/value conflict preserved for G7.
Reported values of $739,320 fixed cost and $701,700 annual operation cost for the paper's assumed booth mix.
A qualitative left-lane modification rather than a new calibrated autonomous-flow model.
A hybrid layout: leftmost straight ETC flow plus the original controlled algorithm for remaining booths and lanes.
A reported elasticity of -1 to mean service time and approximately 0 to variance in the plotted range.
Booth count is reported as the sensitive discrete parameter; speed limit and radius are comparatively insensitive.
A CTM design with two tangent arcs, leading lines, near-even booth allocation, D=105.5 m, and the paper's reported performance/cost values.
A bounded conclusion: inspectable control and simulation benefits coexist with trajectory and data limitations.
A partial reproducibility bridge whose printed comparison operators and one runif call require source-level warning.

moves: input: [ABS Summary] Daily congestion, long commutes, and the post-toll merge motivate a plaza design problem.
rhetorical job: [ABS Summary] Route the reader through assumptions, baseline diagnosis, CTM/WAM construction, comparison, modifications, sensitivity, and closure.
analytical job: [ABS Summary] Keep each promised stage attached to its later metric and avoid treating the route itself as evidence.
output: [ABS Summary] A six-paragraph research-flow abstract that selects CTM in general and announces later reliability checks.
handoff: [ABS Summary] The authority letter converts that pipeline into operational advice and worked values.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [MEM Authority letter] The New Jersey Turnpike Authority needs a safer and more orderly post-toll merge.
rhetorical job: [MEM Authority letter] Diagnose the current plaza, introduce CTM in plain language, report headline efficiency/risk/cost claims, and recommend future construction consideration.
analytical job: [MEM Authority letter] Translate model outputs into an audience decision while preserving the difference between simulation, theory, expectation, and recommendation.
output: [MEM Authority letter] A direct recommendation built around one-second-safe release spacing and a claimed all-aspect advantage.
handoff: [MEM Authority letter] The numbered introduction restates the design task, metrics, and external conditions more formally.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [INT 1 Introduction / 1.1-1.3] Highways require costly infrastructure, toll plazas create merge constraints, and the prompt requests shape, size, pattern, comparison, and adaptation.
rhetorical job: [INT 1 Introduction / 1.1-1.3] Move from public relevance to a typed task and then use literature to accept or reject design principles.
analytical job: [INT 1 Introduction / 1.1-1.3] Identify B and L, three evaluation axes, autonomous/payment extensions, and the barrier and lane-placement choices inherited from prior work.
output: [INT 1 Introduction / 1.1-1.3] A three-paragraph chain: three-objective context -> formal deliverables -> literature-based design decisions.
handoff: [INT 1 Introduction / 1.1-1.3] The assumptions convert those deliverables into tractable motion, arrival, and service premises.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [ASM 2 Assumptions] The real plaza includes heterogeneous behavior, arrivals, acceleration, queues, service times, and vehicle dimensions.
rhetorical job: [ASM 2 Assumptions] List one simplification at a time and usually pair it with a practical reason.
analytical job: [ASM 2 Assumptions] Fix rational lane following, heavy-traffic arrival spacing, simple kinematics, stopped queues, normal human-booth service, and negligible vehicle length.
output: [ASM 2 Assumptions] A conditional operating regime in which the release and merge recurrences can be written.
handoff: [ASM 2 Assumptions] The notation table assigns symbols and units to the retained quantities.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [NOT 3 Notations] The task and assumptions use lane, booth, distance, radius, time, speed, and acceleration quantities.
rhetorical job: [NOT 3 Notations] Create a compact symbol interface before model construction.
analytical job: [NOT 3 Notations] Define L, B, D, d_l, d_b, r, T_h, t_0, v_m, a_s, and a_b with roles and units.
output: [NOT 3 Notations] A reusable symbol table feeding kinematics, geometry, throughput, risk, and cost.
handoff: [NOT 3 Notations] The Models overview consumes the notation to compare EM, CTM, and WAM.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [EM 4.1 Existing Model (EM)] Existing plazas either allow free post-toll merging or assign predefined merge points.
rhetorical job: [EM 4.1 Existing Model (EM)] Give each baseline a fair light-traffic reading before exposing its heavy-traffic failure.
analytical job: [EM 4.1 Existing Model (EM)] Distinguish unpredictability, simultaneous arrival conflict, braking, blockage, and throughput consequences.
output: [EM 4.1 Existing Model (EM)] A diagnosed baseline whose failures motivate a release-time controller rather than only new lane markings.
handoff: [EM 4.1 Existing Model (EM)] Section 4.2 introduces CTM as the direct response to those failures.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [CTM 4.2 Control Time Model (CTM)] The baseline fails because vehicles assigned to one downstream lane may leave neighboring booths too close together.
rhetorical job: [CTM 4.2 Control Time Model (CTM)] Present CTM as an orderly, safer alternative and make the one-second rule, geometry, mapping, and design optimization inspectable.
analytical job: [CTM 4.2 Control Time Model (CTM)] Derive a residual braking time, set t0, simulate throughput, define f and i_k, bound D, and balance booth groups across lanes.
output: [CTM 4.2 Control Time Model (CTM)] A control rule plus a two-arc merge geometry and near-even booth-to-lane allocation; for B=8,L=3, D=105.5 m and three optimal patterns are reported.
handoff: [CTM 4.2 Control Time Model (CTM)] WAM asks whether separating service completion from physical release can recover the waiting time CTM introduces.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [WAM 4.3 Waiting Area Model (WAM)] CTM can keep a serviced vehicle at the booth while it waits for the safe release time.; later in source, [AUTO 6.1 Autonomous-vehicle mixture] The base CTM assumes human driving, while autonomous vehicles may have different lane-recognition and turn behavior.; later in source, [TOLL 6.2 Tollbooth-type proportion] Manual, automatic, and ETC booths have different service mechanisms and capacities.

rhetorical job: [WAM 4.3 Waiting Area Model (WAM)] Treat that occupation as a specific CTM inefficiency and propose a waiting-area variant without claiming it will win.; later in source, [AUTO 6.1 Autonomous-vehicle mixture] Acknowledge the technology's growth, expose a condition-specific risk, and give a simple placement adaptation.; later in source, [TOLL 6.2 Tollbooth-type proportion] Show where CTM remains applicable, where nonstop ETC violates its assumptions, and how to reconfigure the left side.

analytical job: [WAM 4.3 Waiting Area Model (WAM)] Decouple service completion from release, allow the following vehicle to enter service, and defer comparison to throughput analysis.; later in source, [AUTO 6.1 Autonomous-vehicle mixture] Separate the autonomous route from complex curves by assigning it the leftmost straight path.; later in source, [TOLL 6.2 Tollbooth-type proportion] Compare typical service times, use approximately 2000 veh/h ETC capacity, allocate one ETC booth directly to one highway lane, and retain CTM elsewhere.

output: [WAM 4.3 Waiting Area Model (WAM)] A competing CTM variant with a waiting buffer and an explicit later evaluation promise.; later in source, [AUTO 6.1 Autonomous-vehicle mixture] A qualitative left-lane modification rather than a new calibrated autonomous-flow model.; later in source, [TOLL 6.2 Tollbooth-type proportion] A hybrid layout: leftmost straight ETC flow plus the original controlled algorithm for remaining booths and lanes.

handoff: [WAM 4.3 Waiting Area Model (WAM)] Section 5.1 derives parallel recurrences and decides whether the added land is justified.; later in source, [AUTO 6.1 Autonomous-vehicle mixture] Section 6.2 then handles service-technology heterogeneity.; later in source, [TOLL 6.2 Tollbooth-type proportion] Sensitivity analysis next identifies which service and geometry parameters materially affect results.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [THR 5.1 Throughput] EM, CTM, and WAM need a common hourly efficiency measure under manual-booth, two-to-one, heavy-traffic conditions.; later in source, [COST 5.3 Cost] The retained plaza requires land, booth construction, and annual human/automatic operation resources.

rhetorical job: [THR 5.1 Throughput] Define throughput, derive one recurrence per candidate, simulate them in parallel, and use a test plus practical cost to select among them.; later in source, [COST 5.3 Cost] Convert geometry and booth types into fixed and annual cost quantities with one worked example.

analytical job: [THR 5.1 Throughput] Model manual service as N(15,4), add PET delay for EM, impose controlled release recurrences for CTM/WAM, stop at one hour, and compare distributions.; later in source, [COST 5.3 Cost] Use symmetric outer boundaries to estimate area, multiply by land price, add booth construction, and sum annual booth operating terms.

output: [THR 5.1 Throughput] A reported near-tie between EM and CTM, a roughly 1.6 veh/h WAM gain, and a decision to discard WAM because the land cost outweighs the gain.; later in source, [COST 5.3 Cost] Reported values of $739,320 fixed cost and $701,700 annual operation cost for the paper's assumed booth mix.

handoff: [THR 5.1 Throughput] The paper retains CTM and moves to PET-based accident prevention.; later in source, [COST 5.3 Cost] Possible Modification tests whether CTM survives autonomous vehicles and changed booth-type proportions.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [ACC 5.2 Accident prevention] CTM has survived the throughput screen but must be compared with EM on conflict risk.
rhetorical job: [ACC 5.2 Accident prevention] Make safety legible through PET, a probability proxy, simulated distributions, and an accident-rate table.
analytical job: [ACC 5.2 Accident prevention] Define PET severity, posit p=exp(-PET)/100, simulate EM/CTM PET, and convert event probabilities to accidents per 100,000 vehicles.
output: [ACC 5.2 Accident prevention] A claimed 13.66% CTM reduction and one-second PET floor, accompanied by a Table 2 label/value conflict preserved for G7.
handoff: [ACC 5.2 Accident prevention] The next section estimates land, booth, and operating cost for the retained design.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [STH 7.1 Throughput sensitivity] Hourly throughput depends on the service-time distribution parameters used by the simulation.; later in source, [SCOST 7.2 Fixed-cost sensitivity] Fixed cost is determined by geometry, booth count, speed, turning radius, and unit prices.

rhetorical job: [STH 7.1 Throughput sensitivity] Define sensitivity, display mean/variance perturbations, and reconcile the plot with the approximate inverse relation.; later in source, [SCOST 7.2 Fixed-cost sensitivity] Use a three-panel sensitivity figure to identify the main construction-cost lever and qualify less influential geometric parameters.

analytical job: [STH 7.1 Throughput sensitivity] Vary T and sigma, compare elasticities, and identify mean service time as the dominant throughput parameter.; later in source, [SCOST 7.2 Fixed-cost sensitivity] Perturb B, v_m, and r around the stated initial tuple, compute elasticities, and connect booth additions to a cost-efficiency tradeoff.

output: [STH 7.1 Throughput sensitivity] A reported elasticity of -1 to mean service time and approximately 0 to variance in the plotted range.; later in source, [SCOST 7.2 Fixed-cost sensitivity] Booth count is reported as the sensitive discrete parameter; speed limit and radius are comparatively insensitive.

handoff: [STH 7.1 Throughput sensitivity] The fixed-cost branch tests booth count, speed, and turning radius.; later in source, [SCOST 7.2 Fixed-cost sensitivity] Conclusion converts the selected CTM and sensitivity boundaries into one design specification.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [CON 8 Conclusion] The paper has generated EM, CTM, and WAM, screened them by throughput, then analyzed CTM by safety, cost, modifications, and sensitivity.
rhetorical job: [CON 8 Conclusion] Turn the full chain into a concrete plaza specification and restate the worked B=8,L=3 values.
analytical job: [CON 8 Conclusion] Discard WAM, identify EM defects, retain CTM, summarize geometry, pattern, area, throughput, risk, fixed cost, and annual operation cost.
output: [CON 8 Conclusion] A CTM design with two tangent arcs, leading lines, near-even booth allocation, D=105.5 m, and the paper's reported performance/cost values.
handoff: [CON 8 Conclusion] Strengths and Weaknesses calibrates the recommendation before references and code.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [SW 9 Strengths and Weaknesses] The selected CTM needs an explicit credibility and applicability assessment.
rhetorical job: [SW 9 Strengths and Weaknesses] List strengths first, then acknowledge trajectory, failure, arrival-process, and parameter-data weaknesses with partial remedies.
analytical job: [SW 9 Strengths and Weaknesses] Separate structural advantages from realism assumptions and missing empirical calibration.
output: [SW 9 Strengths and Weaknesses] A bounded conclusion: inspectable control and simulation benefits coexist with trajectory and data limitations.
handoff: [SW 9 Strengths and Weaknesses] References support context and the Appendix exposes the simulation algorithms.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

moves: input: [APP Appendix / R code] The main text reports simulation outputs whose event logic should be inspectable.
rhetorical job: [APP Appendix / R code] Expose one implementation path for EM, CTM, WAM efficiency and EM/CTM PET simulation.

analytical job: [APP Appendix / R code] Retain initialization, random service draws, queue ordering, recurrence branches, one-hour stops, and output vectors without treating code syntax as prose style.
output: [APP Appendix / R code] A partial reproducibility bridge whose printed comparison operators and one runif call require source-level warning.
handoff: [APP Appendix / R code] The artifact warning pass reconciles equations, claims, tables, and code before transaction closure.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Retain input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff; put formula and applicability warnings last.

main_argument_chains.claim: CTM converts simultaneous or unpredictable post-toll merging into a controlled release sequence.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat CTM as a candidate controller only after re-deriving its timing proof and testing failure modes.

main_argument_chains.claim: The source's throughput screen finds CTM near EM and WAM only slightly higher.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use an equivalence/noninferiority design and land-cost accounting before selecting a model.

main_argument_chains.claim: The PET risk section is intended to favor CTM but contains a row/value direction conflict.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not transfer the 13.66% claim until table labels and executable aggregation are reconciled.

main_argument_chains.claim: The worked CTM geometry and cost ledger support a conditional B=8,L=3 design description.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Freeze one-direction/two-direction and booth-label conventions before procurement decisions.

main_argument_chains.claim: Autonomous and ETC modifications define applicability boundaries rather than validated new models.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Jointly redesign and simulate the mixed technology case before deployment.

main_argument_chains.claim: Sensitivity plots identify service mean and booth count as local levers but do not establish global reliability.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Add interaction, uncertainty, and decision-switch tests before using the plots as robustness evidence.

warnings.warning: Equation (1) uses actor labels and integration bounds that do not close the stated residual-braking derivation.
The conclusion t0>=t_res is retained, but the displayed derivation does not establish the chosen one-second value without a consistent bound.
The displayed t_i_k approximately T/i_k relation decreases with i_k, while the prose says it increases.
The mapping and minimax geometry are source-specific; no general proof covers all B,L assignments.
EM's appendix rnorm(...,15,4) treats 4 as a standard deviation while prose calls it variance 4.
The CTM recurrence is reconstructed from code; source text omits a complete indexed recurrence and the code uses damaged comparison glyphs in extraction.
WAM defines both t_as and t_bs as lane-b waiting and its appendix initializes runif(1,0,) without an upper bound.
The source 0.0348 value is a one-tail area; a conventional two-tail value is approximately 0.0696.
The 'later two models' prose repeats EM and CTM although the values and 1.6 veh/h statement point to CTM and WAM.
Equation (2) is visually p=exp(-PET)/100; the negative sign is absent from the text layer and the function is uncalibrated.
The risk appendix does not implement the claimed 4,000 repetitions or the Table 2 aggregation.
The literal area expression and the reported one-direction area differ by a global factor of two.
The fixed-cost display writes c_1 while the definition and substitution write c_l; booth h/a labels also conflict.
The printed annual formula contains undefined c'_2 and omits the p_a term needed to reproduce 701,700.
The reconstructed annual-cost substitution is a transparent repair record, not a source formula.
The approximately 2,000 veh/h ETC capacity is an uncalibrated source assertion and does not close a mixed-flow capacity model.
The inverse throughput relation and Figure 10 imply elasticity -1 even though the prose says constant 1.
